title: Molecular analogue of the perovskite repeating unit and evidence for direct MnIII–CeIV–MnIII exchange coupling pathway

material_class.structural_family: perovskite-like {CeIVMnIII8O8} cube with two external CeIII ions

synthesis.procedure: Comproportionation of Mn(O2CPh)2·2H2O, Ce(NO3)3·6H2O, n-Bu4NMnO4, and PhCO2H in a 4:4:1:16 molar ratio in MeNO2 at ~80 °C gave a dark brown solution from which [Ce3Mn8O8(O2CPh)18(HO2CPh)2] was isolated as black crystals (~55% yield based on Mn). Single-crystal X-ray diffraction at 100 K confirmed the structure; metal oxidation states and oxygen protonation levels were assigned from charge balance and bond-valence sums.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution comproportionation; crystallization from the reaction mixture
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: dark brown solution yielded black crystals of Ce3Mn8

properties.summary: Solid-state dc susceptibility of Ce3Mn8 (eicosane-restrained microcrystals, 1 kG, 5–300 K) shows χMT rising from 26.80 cm3 K mol−1 at 300 K to 32.68 cm3 K mol−1 at 30 K then falling to 12.41 cm3 K mol−1 at 5 K, consistent with dominant ferromagnetic MnIII–MnIII pairwise couplings and a C-type antiferromagnetic S = 0 Mn8 cube plus two essentially non-interacting CeIII ions. Ac χM′T down to 1.8 K extrapolates toward ~1.62 cm3 K mol−1 expected for two independent CeIII ions. Fit of χMT to a multi-spin Heisenberg model gave J1 = +1.26 meV (+10.2 cm−1), J2 = +0.69 meV (+5.6 cm−1), J3 = −0.74 meV (−6.0 cm−1), and D = −0.05 meV (−0.40 cm−1), reproducing the C-AF-I ground state; DFT indicated an additional direct MnIII–CeIV–MnIII exchange channel via unoccupied Ce 4f orbitals.
